title: Quote every expansion and build commands with arrays so spaces and newlines stay inside their one argument
summary: Bash splits unquoted expansions on whitespace, so a variable holding 'a b' or an empty-looking-but-present value silently becomes several arguments or vanishes. The fix is to double-quote every expansion and, when composing a command to run, push the arguments into an array and execute that array as one unit instead of reassembling a string.
technique: Store a command as an array, optionally prefix it (bash -x ahead of user args), wrap it in further wrappers, then run exactly that array with quoted slices; the values with spaces/newlines travel intact. Never rebuild the command string by hand.
evidence_note: bin/queue-dev-timeout:67 builds `cmd=("$@")`, composes `runner=(timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after="${kill_after}s" "${timeout_sec}s" "${cmd[@]}")`, then runs `"${runner[@]}"`. queuebash.sh:96 uses `"${matches[@]}"` after a read loop.
invariants: Double-quote every variable, array-slice and $( ) substitution you pass as an argument.
Compose commands-to-run as arrays and expand them quoted ("${cmd[@]}"), never by string concatenation.
Quote $@ in place: "$@", "${*:...}" for the forms you actually need.
Know the difference between ${arr[@]} (each element one word) and ${arr[*]} (joined by IFS).
